newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia seen boosting France uranium sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia seen boosting France uranium sales.

text.p: Australia appears set to increase its uranium exports to France, a government official said on Thursday.
Australia's Liberal-National government said France had met the first requirement by signing the global nuclear test ban treaty in New York on Wednesday.

If other conditions are met, Australia "was back in business," ending an eight-year ban on new contracts with France, a spokesman for the Minister for Primary Resources and Energy, Warwick Parer, told Reuters. "It really does say we're back in the uranium market," he said.
France's signing of the test ban treaty opens the door for more Australian uranium producers to export to France, the spokesman said.
The ban on new uranium contracts was imposed in 1988 when France continued to carry out nuclear tests in the South Pacific.

Foreign Affairs spokesman Peter Collins said the government would be reviewing the uranium policy following France's signature of the treaty, although he would not put a timeframe on when this would happen.

"The government will be reviewing the state of policy in regards to uranium sales and contracts with France in light of this (treaty)," a spokesman for Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer told Reuters.
However, no immediate action on any revision to the government's uranium export policy was planned, he said.
"There is no timeframe as such," he said.
